column1: # qa_011_street_persp: S04 Ruelle des Gourmets street-perspective repaint (2026-10-21). Hooks rewritten to match the new paintings exactly
# and HOOK_STANDARD rule 4 cognate twists. Not merged; do not run finalize/assign until reviewed.
dévorer|devour, day-RAY|Like English 'devour', said day-voh-RAY: a ravenous wolf DEVOURS a whole plate of sausages, lit up by a bright sun RAY.|s|
pique-niquer|peek, key|Like English 'picnic', said peek-nee-KAY: a hedgehog family PICNICS on a checked cloth, one PEEKS round holding up a golden KEY.|s|
consommer|cone, so, may|Like English 'consume', said kohn-soh-MAY: a caterpillar in a party CONE hat CONSUMES leaf after leaf on the balcony.|s|
diluer|dilute|Like English 'dilute', said dee-LWAY (no 't'): grandma tips her watering can into a jug of thick red juice to DILUTE it.|o|
savourer|savour, hooray|Like English 'savour', said sah-voo-RAY: a tortoise SAVOURS a giant strawberry while a party popper bursts 'hoo-RAY!'.|s|
découper|coo, pay|Contains couper (cut), said day-koo-PAY: a girl CUTS OUT paper doves with big scissors and they COO as they flutter off the table.|s|
rôtir|rotisserie|Like 'rotisserie', said roh-TEER: a wide-eyed cook on the rooftop ROASTS a whole chicken on a spit over leaping flames.|o|
rassasier|rah-sah-ZYAY cheer|Two cheerleading ducks shake pom-poms and chant 'RA-SA-ZAY!' (rah-sah-ZYAY) beside a bear sitting on the roof, FULL UP and beaming.|o|
mêler|melee|In a MELEE (may-LAY) two boys plunge brushes into one bucket and the red and yellow paints get MIXED together.|o|
déguster|gusty|A GUSTY wind (day-GEWS-tay) swirls round a lady in a big hat, perched on a ledge, who SAVOURS her slice of tart bite by bite.|o|
engouffrer|goofy|A GOOFY floppy-eared dog (ahn-GOO-fray) GOBBLES UP a whole plate of food in one go, nose buried in the dish.|o|
trinquer|drink? OK!|Said TRAN-KAY, like 'DRINK? OK!': two friends on a little red balcony call it out and CLINK GLASSES.|o|
désaltérer|dazzle, Terry|By the DAZZLING gold knob on a sun-baked teapot roof, thirsty TERRY (day-ZAHL-tay-RAY) QUENCHES HIS THIRST, gulping a tall glass of cool water.|o|
ailler|aye-aye|A pirate cheers 'AYE-AYE!' (ah-YAY), waving a fat GARLIC bulb over the GARLICKY toast he is munching.|o|

farcir|far-seer|A FAR-SEER (fahr-SEER) stargazer peers through her brass telescope from inside a giant STUFFED-tomato house, a bowl of rice stuffing at her feet, and checks herself in an oval MIRROR (se farcir).|o|
cuisiner|queasy, neigh|A QUEASY-looking horse in an apron, mouth wide, goes 'NEIGH!' (kwee-zee-NAY) as it COOKS a steaming meal at the stove.|w|
